acceptance_criteria: A test connection against a self-signed Palo Alto certificate succeeds, proven by a test replacing the prior 'untrusted chain fails' assertion

baseline.authority: docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_21_PAN_TLS_VERIFICATION_DISABLED.md (RATIFIED, 2026-09-21), which supersedes AGENTS.md's Palo Alto TLS clause for this deployment and directs that PanXmlApiTransport accept whatever certificate a Palo Alto device presents, with no chain verification and no per-device enrollment step.
baseline.engineering: PanXmlApiTransport.paloAltoDeviceTrustManager currently: tries chain verification first, then a per-device stored/pinned fingerprint, then rejects as UnverifiableCertificateException carrying only the fingerprint. This movement removes the rejection path entirely for the no-verification case; a device certificate is accepted once presented, still subject to basic X.509 structural validity (not expired, well-formed) but not to chain trust or fingerprint matching.
baseline.observed: NXS-LOCAL-0359 (chain verification) and NXS-LOCAL-0363 (per-device certificate enrollment) are both live. Every one of the 39 enumerated Palo Alto devices in this internal-only environment presents its own self-signed certificate, so every connection reports unverifiable and requires an enrollment the Product Owner has decided is unwanted friction for this environment. This movement reverses that behaviour for Palo Alto specifically, per the ratified decision.
